reason: Reflowed the closed-choice native expansion sentence without changing its meaning; the existing skill assertion and the shipped choice-detail reference remain valid. Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for closed-choice descriptions and the recommended choice. ask and send gain --choice-description (attached to the --choice just before it) and --recommended <label>; ask --form choices may be objects with label, description and recommended. The Claude Code picker bridge now carries option descriptions on the device choices and turns the one "(Recommended)" label suffix into the recommended choice; the Body keeps only wording too long for a device. The use_question_picker suggestion carries descriptions and the suffix; a question with descriptions or a recommendation keeps ordinary ask instead of the Codex card, which shows labels only. The skill points closed choices at send-details.md, which teaches the flags; the harness-claude-code reference says devices show descriptions on the choices. The shipped questions topic is unchanged: it already says closed choices carry their own consequence, and the default owner context has no byte headroom left. Protocol: ReplyChoice description and recommended, pushes carry descriptions only when they fit, and content responses carry the questions. Earlier on this branch, kept: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for the Cursor activation follow-up. It is now sent at most once per conversation, recorded by conversation id outside session state, because the Cursor SDK starts and ends a session around every turn and each new session re-armed it. Its text now opens by saying it is an automatic activation not from the User, carries the same root ownership and effective guidance, and closes by asking the agent to evaluate the turn it just finished and then repeat its previous reply exactly instead of acknowledging the activation, since hosts such as T3 Code show only that reply. The README and the Cursor harness reference say the same. No command, flag, readiness id, hook definition or guidance topic changed. Earlier on main, kept: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for one comment-only change: the note in the hook builder that explains why the Session Child's attend handler stays a separate asynchronous handler now records the harness behaviour behind it (a process left by a synchronous hook is reparented to init, the hub refuses it as not the harness's child, Codex ends a session by killing its async hooks and never kills such a process, Claude Code kills neither and does not time out a backgrounded hook). No hook definition, command, flag, readiness id or guidance wording changed. Earlier on main, kept: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for two fixes. A Codex hook refresh keeps the revision its handlers already carry, so an update that adds one handler leaves every unchanged handler byte-identical and Codex asks the User to review only the new or changed one; the updates reference already says changed handlers can require /hooks approval, which stays true, and the activation proof still accepts a callback from the healthy definition present. Rollback, a stable downgrade and an npm switch to a release before 13.1.0-beta.3 now rewrite exec-form Claude Code hooks to shell form before that release becomes active, and activate or install nothing when that fails, reporting it with `notifai doctor --json` as the recovery command; agents still run the same update and rollback commands and follow the reported recovery command, so no command, flag, readiness id or guidance wording changed. Earlier on main, kept: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for two small CLI changes. `config set --project` for a key that widens network trust (media_origins, approve_origins) now gives the trust-specific refusal wherever it runs, including outside a Git checkout, instead of the generic shared-settings refusal; both already name `--local`. `notifai config` for humans aligns each group's names on their own and continues a long value under itself, so no row is wider than the terminal; the plain and JSON forms are unchanged. No agent-facing behaviour, command, flag, readiness id or guidance wording changed.
